title: Mesons, Confinement, and Complexity: A Krylov Space Perspective on the Long-Range Ising Chain
authors: Xuhao Jiang, Jad C. Halimeh, N. S. Srivatsa
abstract: We investigate the interplay between confinement and Krylov complexity in the long-range transverse-field Ising chain, where power-law interactions $\sim 1/r^α$ generate an effective confining potential between domain walls without an explicit symmetry-breaking field. Using the time-averaged Krylov state complexity after a quench as a diagnostic, we find that the complexity is strongly suppressed and only weakly system size-dependent at small $α$ and small transverse field $h_x$, where confinement is strongest, and crosses over to rapid growth at larger $α$, where it increases with system size. Within the confined regime, the oscillation frequencies of the complexity agree with the meson masses of an effective two-kink model, with the dominant frequency growing linearly with the lightest meson mass and the time-averaged complexity decreasing approximately as its inverse square. We further study operator Krylov complexity at finite temperature using the Wightman inner product. At low temperature, it exhibits bounded oscillations that directly encode the meson spectrum, whereas this structure is progressively washed out as the temperature increases. These results identify Krylov complexity as a spectroscopic probe of interaction-induced confinement and reproduce, in a microscopic lattice model, the hallmarks of Krylov complexity identified in confining field theories.
summary: This work uses Krylov complexity as a novel diagnostic tool to study confinement in the long-range transverse-field Ising chain. By analyzing the time evolution of state and operator complexity, the authors successfully link the complexity's spectral features to the meson masses arising from the effective two-kink model. This confirms complexity as a robust probe for interaction-induced confinement in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how confinement, arising from long-range interactions in the transverse-field Ising chain, can be diagnosed using Krylov complexity measures.
main_result: Krylov complexity serves as a spectroscopic probe, showing that its oscillations encode the meson spectrum in the confined regime ($\alpha < 2$).
method: The study employs Krylov state and operator complexity, calculated via the Lanczos algorithm, to analyze quantum dynamics after a quench or at finite temperature.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional long-range transverse-field Ising chain with Hamiltonian $\hat{H}(\alpha, h_x) = -\sum_{i<j} J r^{\alpha}_{ij} \sigma^z_i \sigma^z_j - h_x \sum_{i=1}^L \sigma^x_i$. Confinement is induced by the power-law decay $\sim 1/r^\alpha$ without an explicit symmetry-breaking field.
key_observables: Krylov State Complexity ($C_{KS}(t)$), Operator Krylov Complexity ($C_{KO}(t)$), and the meson masses derived from the power spectrum of $C_{KS}(t)$.
important_parameters: The exponent $\alpha$ controls confinement ($\alpha < 2$ is strongly confined), the transverse field $h_x$, and the temperature $T$ (or inverse temperature $ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the dynamics onto the Krylov subspace and using the time-averaged complexity as a diagnostic tool.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Fourier spectrum of $C_{KS}(t)$ showing peaks at meson masses, and show the dependence of $C_{KS}$ on $\alpha$ and $h_x$, highlighting the crossover between confined and deconfined regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the state complexity after a quench, linking its oscillations to meson masses. It then extends this to operator complexity at finite temperature, demonstrating how the spectral structure is preserved at low $T$ but washed out at high $T$.
why_interesting: The use of complexity measures to diagnose fundamental physical phenomena like confinement and bound states provides a powerful, non-perturbative diagnostic tool applicable across different quantum many-body systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Fourier spectrum of the Krylov state complexity CKS(t) and meson masses in the long-range Ising model. The background shows log10[PK(ω)/PK,max] for L = 16 and hx = 0.30, with PK(ω) defined in Eq. (3). The discrete Fourier transform is performed over 0 ≤t ≤2000 with a time step of ∆t = 0.05. White curves show the finite-size two-kink levels m1,2,3 [19], solid where the level is a meson and dashed where it is a discretized scattering state, while colored markers indicate the spectral peaks assigned to the mesons; the weakest m3 peaks lie below the color scale. The inset shows CKS(t) for two selected values of α.

FIG. 2. Time-averaged Krylov state complexity CKS(α, hx) over the time window t ∈[0, 200] following a quench from a fully polarized initial state under the long-range Hamiltonian ˆH(α, hx) [Eq. (1)], shown on a logarithmic color scale for system sizes (a) L = 12, (b) L = 14, and (c) L = 16. The dashed line marks α = 2, the threshold beyond which the long-range confining potential is known to saturate at large domain-wall separation [10]. For α ≲2 the complexity is suppressed by up to two orders of magnitude and depends only weakly on system size L, whereas at large α it grows rapidly and increases with L.

FIG. 3. (a) Time-averaged Krylov state complexity CKS, scaled by Lh2 x, versus the lightest meson mass m1 for L = 12, 14, and 16. The dashed line is the leading-order result 2/m2 1. (b) Dominant oscillation frequency ωd of CKS(t) versus m1 for L = 16. The dashed line marks ωd = m1. In both panels, 1.1 ≤α ≤2, hx = 0.2 and 0.3, and time averages are taken over the time window t ∈[0, 200].

FIG. 4. Operator Krylov dynamics of the domain wall-number operator ˆODW in the long-range transverse-field Ising chain with L = 13, hx = 0.3, and α = 1.4, for a range of inverse temperatures β. The operator Krylov basis contains at most Kmax = 5000 basis operators; numerical details are given in the Supplemental Material [19]. (a) Operator Krylov complexity CKO(t). Its approximately linear growth slows as β increases. Inset: short-time view at large β, where CKO(t) oscillates and approaches the single-meson prediction sin2(m1t).
